name: Hua Hin
coordsNote: Hua Hin town centre near the beach and night market; condos stretch south towards Khao Takiab.

english.note: Good in town (expat hub — above national average)
english.rationale: Thailand is a low-proficiency country on the EF EPI 2025 (score 402, rank 116; country tier 1). Hua Hin has a decades-old Scandinavian, British and German retiree and snowbird community, with condo management, hospitals and services used to English, so +1 for an expat hub. Thinner than Bangkok or Chiang Mai outside the tourist core.

vibe: Royal seaside town, golf, night markets, retiree long-stayers
narrative: The royal family's long-time seaside retreat, about three hours from Bangkok: a long sandy beach running south to Khao Takiab, night markets, golf courses and a deep stock of condos built around winter long-stayers. Calmer and cheaper than Phuket, but the Gulf beaches are flatter and less dramatic, and dedicated coworking is thin.

season.rationale: Editorial estimate. Foreign high season is Nov–Feb (snowbirds stay into March), peaking Dec–Feb. Bangkok weekenders keep a domestic base all year, with Songkran in April and the Jazz City event at the end of May. Jul–Aug pick up on European family holidays. May–Jun and Sep–Oct are the lowest, and the best time to negotiate leases.

sources.title: I Am Koh Chang — Cost to live in Hua Hin
sources.note: Page also gives Low Season (May to October) as the 'best time for negotiating long-term leases'.

swim.name: Gulf of Thailand (Hua Hin beach)
swim.note: Warm all year (27–30 °C). Jellyfish risk is highest in the May–Oct rainy season, so swim at lifeguarded stretches

source.title: seatemperatu.re — Hua Hin, best time to swim
source.note: January is the coldest month (~27 °C); 'ideal swimming' every month. Jellyfish note from FCDO Thailand safety page.

safety.propertyNote: Low crime resort town; minor scams and opportunistic theft
safety.womensSafetyNote: Generally safe; quiet family and retiree town
safety.touristRationale: Resort town with a mostly older, long-stay visitor base; no sign of visitor-targeted crime beyond the petty theft already in the property score.

rationale.property: Small, family- and retiree-oriented royal resort town without Patong-style nightlife; the usual bag-snatching and overcharging guidance (FCDO, country-wide) applies. Set level with Chiang Mai (74), above Bangkok (62) and Phuket (66).
rationale.tourist: No evidence of a visitor-vs-local risk gap; 1.0 as for other Thai cities.
rationale.womens: FCDO's Thai warnings (drink spiking, assaults) centre on party areas; Hua Hin's bar scene is small and the town is family- and retiree-oriented. Modest +5 over the country Gallup baseline, below Chiang Mai's legacy +10.

consulted.title: U.S. State Department travel advisories (official data feed)
consulted.note: Prachuap Khiri Khan is not in the higher-caution areas (Thai-Cambodian border; Yala, Pattani, Narathiwat).

consulted.title: UK FCDO — Thailand safety and security
consulted.quote: Jellyfish can swim close to the shore, particularly during the rainy season from May to October.

consulted.title: U.S. State Department travel advisories RSS feed (official)

selection: Gulf-coast snowbird town long favoured by Scandinavian and other retirees; dry Dec–Apr, with monsoon timing different from Phuket (rainiest Sep–Nov). Comparables: Chiang Mai, Da Nang, Nha Trang.
researchNotes: No hazard flagged: Hua Hin is one of the drier stretches of the Thai coast and its Sep–Nov rains are not a safety hazard; the climate pipeline already scores rain days. The US advisory's area risks (armed conflict near the Cambodian border, unrest in the deep south) are listed as the page names them; they do not apply to Hua Hin. travel.state.gov was behind a bot check, so the text came from cadataapi.state.gov. The 'royal retreat' and 'three hours from Bangkok' claims are general knowledge plus nomads.com's 3-hour figure; coworking thinness is per nomads.com and digitalnomads.world. Loy Krathong is omitted for lack of a Hua Hin-specific source.
